title: Désirée's Baby

teacherSummary.text: Désirée, a foundling raised by the Valmondés, marries the proud planter Armand Aubigny. When their baby begins to show African ancestry, Armand turns cold and sends her away; she walks with the baby into the bayou and does not return. Burning her things, Armand finds a letter from his own mother, revealing that she belonged to 'the race that is cursed with the brand of slavery.'

satQuestions.passage: It was no wonder, when she stood one day against the stone pillar in whose shadow she had lain asleep, eighteen years before, that Armand Aubigny riding by and seeing her there, had fallen in love with her. segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “it means that you are not white” slowly and put it in my own words: Désirée, frightened, asks her husband what it means that he says she is not white. Next, craft. I notice the sentence is short and plain, but it carries the whole weight of the story's racial law. The strongest word is “white”: everything in her world, marriage, safety, love, depends on this one label. Then, effect. What is Désirée really asking Armand when she repeats these words? My answer: When Désirée repeats Armand's words, she is really asking whether he believes she is not white and whether he still loves her; the line shows how quickly a racial label can destroy her place and his love.
